The activities are described and their results are evaluated in terms of services rendered and variations in total and abortion-related maternal mortality between 2010 and 2014.
Materials and methods
The Provincial Sexual and Reproductive Health Program developed two main strategies for reducing abortion-related maternal mortality [4].
(1) A risk and harm reduction strategy in primary health care with general physicians and midwives, with the support of secondary care (started in 2007). (2) The provision of legal termination of pregnancy (LTP) services, also in primary health care in the same medical centers, since 2012, with the assistance of the Argentine Federation of Societies of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FASGO) and FIGO.

decisions.reason: Matía et al. (2016) describe and evaluate the public health policies implemented by the Province of Buenos Aires Ministry of Health through the Provincial Sexual and Reproductive Health Program (PSSR), combining primary-care risk and harm reduction counseling (started in 2007 and modeled on 'Iniciativas Sanitarias' in Uruguay) with primary-care legal termination of pregnancy (LTP) services (started in 2012) and manual vacuum aspiration training (started in 2014). The paper reports descriptive 2010–2015 service provision counts across four municipalities and provincial maternal and abortion-related mortality trends from 2010 to 2014. Although the title and text refer to 'replicating the Uruguayan risk and harm reduction model' and discuss transferability to primary care, this refers to adopting and transferring a clinical service delivery model into a new public policy setting rather than conducting an empirical test of a specific prior published mortality claim. The shipped original study, Briozzo et al. (2006) (10.1016/j.ijgo.2006.07.013), is never cited in the text or reference list (only Briozzo & Faúndes, 2008 [Ref. 6] is cited in the Discussion regarding health professionals' willingness to provide legal abortion services), and the authors explicitly note that provincial maternal mortality reductions cannot be credited to the evaluated primary health units alone. Under the Codebook, transferring a clinical/policy service model without empirically retesting a prior published research finding is not_a_replication.

decisions.reason: Krupnikov and Piston (2015) develop and test a novel theoretical model (Hypotheses 1 and 2, p. 156) predicting that the effect of campaign negativity on candidate evaluations and turnout is jointly conditioned by candidate race and White voters' racial attitudes (prejudice and sympathy), using a national survey experiment (N = 737, p. 157) with text-based news-story stimuli adapted from Brooks & Geer (2007) and an internal 'replication study' (Study 2, N = 271, p. 164) repeating their own main experiment with modified racial-attitude timing and scales. The shipped original study, Kahn and Geer (1994), is cited only twice: once in Theory (p. 155, alongside Lau & Rovner, 2009 and Fridkin & Kenney, 2011) as general background literature noting that going negative carries a backlash risk, and once in Experimental Results (p. 158) in a single introductory sentence ('Consistent with past research (Kahn & Geer, 1994), we find that sponsoring a negative advertisement leads to a penalty (Figure 2a)') before testing their three-way interaction hypotheses. Just as the authors cite Lau et al. (2007) and Goldstein & Freedman (2002) for baseline turnout comparisons (pp. 162–163) and Lau & Rovner (2009) in the Conclusion (p. 166) for the general negativity penalty, reporting that a baseline main effect aligns with consensus literature while testing a new moderation theory is a literature consistency check, not an empirical replication of Kahn and Geer's (1994) television advertising study.

Metacognitive therapy (MCT; Wells, 2009) was developed to reduce the CAS and to modify underlying maladaptive metacognitive beliefs. MCT has been found to be an effective treatment for depression and several anxiety disorders (Normann et al., 2014), but has yet to be evaluated in its purer form in SAD.
We therefore aimed to conduct a preliminary investigation of the efficacy of MCT for SAD using single case methodology. Following the generic MCT conceptualization and treatment structure (Wells, 2009), we aimed to test if MCT could be applied using a single-case replication methodology that spanned cases of increasing complexity. decisions.reason: Nordahl and Wells (2018) conduct a preliminary evaluation of generic Metacognitive Therapy (MCT; Wells, 2009) for Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD) across three patients of increasing clinical complexity using an A–B single-case design. The term 'Replication Series' in the title and 'systematic replication (Barlow and Hersen, 1984)' in the Introduction and Materials and Methods refer to within-study single-case replication across the three patients to establish generalizability across SAD subtypes. The shipped original study, Wells and Papageorgiou (2001) (a brief cognitive therapy case series based on Clark and Wells's 1995 cognitive model), is cited only once in the entire paper (Introduction, alongside Nordahl et al., 2016b) as background contrast: the authors explain that those earlier abbreviated treatments relied on the CBT model, included testing negative thoughts, and omitted core MCT components, whereas generic MCT 'has yet to be evaluated in its purer form in SAD.' Wells and Papageorgiou (2001) is never mentioned or compared in the Methods, Results, or Discussion. Under the Codebook, evaluating a distinct, previously untested pure-MCT intervention protocol with internal across-case repetition is not_a_replication.

decisions.reason: Konowal et al. (2026) evaluate an organizational behavior management (OBM) supervisor training and dresser job-aid intervention for direct service providers (DSPs) across five residential students with autism and intellectual disability ('A Five-Case Replication Series') to address parent complaints that students wore other students' clothing rather than their own personal clothing. While the Introduction reviews three prior clothing-related studies—Nutter and Reid (1978), McClannahan et al. (1990), and Buckley et al. (2025) (which evaluated a care-provider checklist and visual-cue intervention for general clothing appearance and personal hygiene)—and notes that 'Like McClannahan et al. (1990) and Buckley et al. (2025), the present five-case replication series did not focus directly on teaching students dressing skills, rather evaluated the effects of training care providers to monitor and assist the students wearing personal clothing,' the authors explicitly state that their objective was 'to evaluate the effectiveness of training on a facet of clothing appearance not studied previously' and reiterate in Treatment Implications that 'evaluation of procedures to overcome these problems has not been researched previously.' The 'five-case replication series' refers to repeating the intervention across five students within this study, not empirically retesting Buckley et al. (2025); thus, under the Codebook, type is not_a_replication.

decisions.reason: Kohannim et al. (2012) introduce a gene-centric LASSO regression and multi-SNP partial F-test method to discover gene associations with MRI-derived temporal lobe volume in the ADNI dataset (N = 729), identifying 22 genome-wide significant genes led by a novel hit in MACROD2 (p = 7.94 x 10^-12), and then test and partially replicate their own newly discovered MACROD2 association in an independent cohort of 564 healthy young Australian twins and siblings. Under the Codebook, validating a novel discovery made within the same paper in a second cohort is an internal discovery-and-replication design (not_a_replication). Nor is the ADNI analysis a reproduction of the shipped original study, Stein et al. (2010a) (univariate GWAS of temporal lobe volume in ADNI): Stein et al. (2010a) is used strictly as a methodological detection-power benchmark (alongside Hibar et al., 2011a) to show that multi-SNP LASSO boosts gene-level p-values for GRIN2B and NRXN3 (from 10^-7 and 10^-6 to 10^-9 and 10^-8) and detects 20 additional genes whose individual SNPs failed univariate significance, while yielding a weaker association for sub-threshold univariate candidate ADAMTS2. Neither GRIN2B nor NRXN3 is tested in the independent Brisbane cohort. Per the Codebook, applying a new statistical method to an existing dataset for novel discovery while benchmarking against prior univariate hits is not_a_replication.

decisions.reason: Benegas and Sirur Flores (2014) conduct an original longitudinal evaluation of using two electric-circuit units from the curriculum 'Tutorials in Introductory Physics' (McDermott, Shaffer, et al., Refs. [5, 23–25]) versus traditional instruction across five 11th-grade classes in private and state-run Argentinean high schools without laboratory facilities, examining immediate learning gains, 1-year retention, novice versus experienced teachers, and gender. Throughout the paper, the authors use 'replication of Tutorials in Introductory Physics' and 'replicate Tutorials teaching as closely as possible to the recommendations [25] of the developing site' to mean implementing the instructional curriculum with pedagogical fidelity in a new educational system, not retesting a specific prior empirical study finding. Prior college Tutorials implementation studies (Refs. [6, 8, 17–20]) are cited only as general background on active learning and local curricular adaptation, and the repetition by two novice teachers in the following school year (Research Question 3) is an internal repetition within this study. Finally, Engelhardt and Beichner (2004) [Ref. 21] is the instrument-development paper for the DIRECT diagnostic test (which did not evaluate Tutorials), and its compound sample's 49% score on the 19 matching items is used solely as an external competency benchmark. Under the Codebook, evaluating a curriculum and assessment instrument in a new setting without targeting a specific prior empirical finding is not_a_replication.
